key_insight: Smaller reported uncertainty did not guarantee accurate molecular VQE energies: hardware execution bias and cross-job variability could dominate.
engineering_relevance: Validate workload-specific bias and repeatability before buying more shots or mitigation, since mitigation gains can carry substantial QPU cost.
method: Evaluate noiselessly optimized molecular VQE states on IBM Aachen and Pittsburgh 156-qubit Heron processors.
Freeze parameters, layouts and compiled circuits, with dynamical decoupling disabled.
Compare raw and mitigated energies across molecular cohorts, repeated windows and known-state controls.
evidence_signal: Across 110 jobs and 28.2 billed QPU minutes, Raw 1024 O2 and BeH2 mean residuals were 12–32 times returned uncertainty; ZNE reduced O2 absolute residuals by 49.7–83.5% at about fourfold charge.
watch_item: Mitigated estimates require physical-validity checks: 13 energy point estimates fell outside the mapped spectrum, versus none for raw estimates.
paper_title: Execution bias, repeatability and mitigation cost in parameter-frozen molecular VQE energy evaluation
